# Bring up a new unit

Revision A has never been built. Do each step in order and stop at the first one that fails.

> [!CAUTION]
> **No memory until the supply is proven**
>
> Do not fit a memory module until you have swept the DUT supply and seen the over-voltage cut-off work.

## Before you order

1. Print each socket footprint at 1:1 and lay the real part on it: 72-pin SIMM, 30-pin SIMM, ZIF sockets and ZIP strips. The SIMM and ZIP patterns come from published dimensions.
2. Check each DIP and ZIP pin map marked `UNVERIFIED` in `spec/ramspec.py` against the manufacturer's datasheet.
3. Check every part number and its stock in the assembler's BOM tool.
4. Check the part rotations in the assembler's placement preview.
5. Check the card-edge socket footprint against the socket you buy. The pattern is from Samtec's drawing for PCIE-164-02-x-D-RA.
6. Order the cartridges with hard-gold fingers and a bevelled tongue.
7. Check that the PD controller you fit (CH224A) has the CH224K pinout the schematic uses.
8. Check the fabricator's limits against the table in [Build a unit](../start/build.md#fabrication-limits).
9. If you fit the Wi-Fi module, check J8 against a real XIAO first. See [Fit the Wi-Fi module](fit-wifi-module.md).

## Base board without power

1. Measure the resistance from each rail to ground: `VBUS`, `+3V3`, `+5V`, `+1V1`, `+2V5`, `RP_1V1` and `VDUT`.
2. Stop if any rail reads as a short.

## Base board, first power

Use a bench supply set to 5 V with a 100 mA limit on `VBUS`.

1. Check that `+3V3`, `+1V1`, `+2V5` and `RP_1V1` are in range and that `+5V` follows the input.
2. Hold BOOT and connect USB. The board appears as a USB drive.
3. Load the firmware.
4. Check that the FPGA configures: `DONE` goes high, the ID register reads `0x52414D31` and the PLL locks.
5. Connect a PD charger. `VBUS` goes to 9 V.
6. Repeat step 5 with several chargers and with a 5 V-only source.

## DUT supply

Test with no cartridge first, then with a dummy load.

1. Sweep the DAC. The output goes from 2.3 V to 5.6 V and falls with every step of the DAC. Record the table.
2. Leave `STRAP_5V_OK` open and raise the output. The switch drops out above about 3.85 V.
3. Ground `STRAP_5V_OK` and raise the output. The switch drops out above about 5.86 V.
4. Measure ripple and step response at 0 A, 1 A and 2 A.
5. Compare the current reading with a meter.
6. Switch the rail on into a cartridge and record the current with a probe. Compare the peak and the rise time with the table below.
7. Force the comparator to trip and measure how long the switch takes to open.
8. Short the output and measure the trip time.
9. Measure the discharge time after switch-off.
10. Measure the switch temperature at 2 A.

## Timing

1. Run the loopback with no [DUT](../reference/glossary.md#term-dut) at 3.0 V, 5.0 V and 5.5 V. Record the launch-to-capture delay of each line.
2. Store that table in the cartridge EEPROM. It is the calibration table.
3. Measure the input-delay step size against one [Tick](../reference/glossary.md#term-tick).
4. Measure RAS to data-valid on a known module with an oscilloscope. Compare it with the access time the tester reports. The target is within 3 ns.
5. Measure edge rates and ground bounce with 36 DQ lines switching.

## Memory

1. Test known-good and known-bad parts in every socket: each size, parity and non-parity, FPM and EDO, 5 V and 3.3 V SIMMs, and each DIP family.
2. For the 4116, watch the three rails on an oscilloscope at power-on and power-off.
3. Pull the -5 V pump and check that +12 V and +5 V stay off.
4. Insert a chip backwards. The current limit trips and nothing overheats.
5. Loop the tests for thirty minutes at the highest current.
6. Repeat on a second unit and compare the results.

## Cartridge slot

1. Check the insertion force and the alignment on the rails.
2. Check that the shell clears the console when the cartridge is seated.
3. Measure the contact resistance of the DUT-rail contacts at 2 A, and their temperature rise.
4. Pull a cartridge with the DUT supply on. The comparator opens the switch within about 0.1 ms, because `STRAP_5V_OK` opens. The firmware does not read `ADP_PRESENT_N` yet, so the regulator stays on.

## Limits of revision A

| Missing | State |
| --- | --- |
| 168-pin SDRAM DIMMs | The base has the lines and the SPD bus. The cartridge and the synchronous engine do not exist. |
| ECC-optimised 72-pin SIMMs | Different pinout, no socket map. |
| Access time from CAS, page-mode cycle time | Not measured separately. |
| EMC | No work done. A unit sold assembled needs it. |

The DUT supply simulation (`hardware/spice/run.sh`) gives the figures to compare with the first board. Measure each one before you plug in a module.

| Measure | Simulated |
| --- | --- |
| Rail at DAC code 0 | 5.600 V. The rail cannot be set higher |
| Comparator trip, `STRAP_5V_OK` open | 3.851 V |
| Comparator trip, `STRAP_5V_OK` grounded | 5.863 V |
| Switch-on into a SIMM cartridge at 5 V | 0.4 A peak. The cartridge reaches 90 % after 1.5 ms |
| Comparator trip to switch open | 0.1 ms |
| Discharge from 5 V | Below 0.5 V after 25 ms |
| Drop to the cartridge at 2 A | 172 mV without the board copper. The regulator senses ahead of the shunt and the switch |

The simulation uses generic transistor models and no wiring inductance. Treat the figures as estimates.

### Open design faults

The simulations in [Study the supplies and the bus](../develop/check.md#study-the-supplies-and-the-bus) report these faults. None is fixed. Each figure is simulated with the models that section names.

| Where | Fault | Simulated |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cartridges | Overshoot at the memory pins | -2.5 V to 7.5 V at 5 V against -1 V and 6 V allowed. 47 Ω in place of 22 Ω brings the worst line inside |
| Cartridges | Strobe edges cross the threshold three times | Nine edges on RAS, CAS and WE at 5 V with a light load. A DRAM can take one edge for two |
| Cartridges | The receive buffers over-drive the FPGA inputs | 5.5 V to 6.2 V at pads rated 3.63 V. A 68 Ω resistor at each buffer output gives 3.41 V |
| DIP cartridge | No soft start on the +5 V switch | 15.4 A peak. The slot's 5 V dips to 1.49 V |
| DIP cartridge | -5 V sags at power-down | -2.2 V while +12 V is still falling. It should hold -4.5 V |
| DIP cartridge | +12 V and VCC come on 0.1 ms before -5 V is in tolerance | -4.28 V at that moment |
| DIP cartridge | -5 V idles at +0.72 V with the supplies off | The comparator's divider pulls it up |
| Base | 5.5 V is not reachable on every unit | 6.7 % of units stop short. The top of the rail spans 5.40 V to 5.78 V |
| Base | The comparator can trip at a legitimate set point | 127 mV below 5.5 V and 194 mV below 3.6 V at the worst corner |
| Base | Low set points are off before any trim | 8.1 % of units are more than 5 % out at 2.6 V. The firmware refuses the rail there and does not trim |
| Base | Input-pad leakage of the RP2350 can close the switch | 120 µA lifts the request line to 1.09 V. The figure is the erratum's, quoted from memory |
| Base | DUT inductor at its limit | 2.50 A peak at a 2 A load. The part saturates at 2.0 A to 2.5 A |
| Base | FPGA core supply | 994 mΩ at 100 MHz against a 220 mΩ target, and 205 mΩ from the regulator to the balls |
| Base | A 5 V-only charger cannot run 5 V tests | 4.55 V at 2 A. The firmware does not read the input voltage |
| Firmware | The DIP cartridge's supply enable is never driven | 4116-type chips cannot be tested yet |

The speed measurement has one more limit. The copper alone differs by up to 1.6 ns between bus lines on a cartridge, and the buffers add 2 ns to 10.7 ns by their datasheets. The engine steps in 3.08 ns, so a line can read one step fast or slow until the delay is calibrated per line.

The regulator cannot pull its output down. After the rail is switched off, the regulator's own capacitors stay charged. In the simulation they fall from 5 V to 3.85 V in 0.7 s. If a 3.3 V cartridge follows a 5 V test at once, the comparator keeps the switch open for that time.
